structured_output.summary: Attempt 2 fixes all five findings from phase attempt 1. compare_union now matches branches by multiplicity (Counter), so duplicated branches show up as extras. Root servers and security are compared explicitly whenever no operation inherits the root in both documents. A new require_coverage net fails any operation or component whose model changed but has no classified change. Changed-type schemas and changed operation security are now scanned, and flow names and keys are validated. A new source lists its operations. Seven new regression tests cover these cases. Every recorded check on source a4afcf07… exits 0, including 53 drift tests, `airs_drift --check`, `--require-through-phase 25` and the SDK-unchanged diff. Three low gaps remain: the coverage net only works per operation or component, a duplicated oneOf branch can be labelled additive, and there is no remote CI evidence yet. Total 46/50.

findings.description: A duplicated branch (old [A,B] → new [A,B,A]) now goes through the prefix-append path and gets the disposition 'additive' (union_variant_appended). Under oneOf, a duplicate makes every value that matches A invalid, so it is a breaking change. The change is still reported as review_required, so nothing is dropped, but it is mislabelled. test_union_duplication_is_classified_even_beside_other_changes (test_airs_drift.py:550) accepts either class.
findings.required_fix: Under oneOf, or whenever an appended extra repeats an existing branch, emit union_variant_inserted or another breaking class. Make the test require that exact class.

findings.description: require_coverage works per operation or component. Inside an operation or component that already has a classified change, it cannot catch a second difference that a compare method drops. Today every model field is compared explicitly, so this is a latent gap, not a reproduced hole. The stronger reconstruction check suggested in attempt 1 was not adopted.
findings.required_fix: Optionally tighten the net to the field level. For example, compare model sub-keys (parameters, requestBody, responses, security, servers, annotations) for each operation, or schema keywords for each component, against the change pointers. Add a mock-dropped-difference test that also carries another classified change in the same operation.

limitations: This was a read-only review: I ran no tests. Execution evidence comes only from the recorded checks file, which I read in part and grepped for the rest. I did not recompute its SHA-256.
No live `refresh` run or remote CI run was inspected. The plan's remote-CI finishing step (plan:262) is not yet evidenced for this source, which is expected after review.
The oneOf-duplication and coverage-granularity findings come from reading the code, not from reproduction.
I did not re-audit the vendor 0.86.0 bytes, historical_delivery.py or red_team_management.py internals beyond their passing recorded checks.
Phase 25's entry in phase-status.json has no acceptance_criteria array, unlike sibling phases. I judged acceptance from the plan's phase 25 section.
